name: Noether’s symmetry and conservation results
description: Noether established a mathematical relationship between continuous symmetries and conservation laws in suitable variational theories.

impact.note: Known to physicists and mathematicians, it explained conservation laws through symmetry and became a foundation for a line of modern field theory.

date.basis: Year of the cited publication or dated report; not necessarily the date work began.

events.statement: Noether published work linking geometric symmetries with conservation laws in 1918.

evidence.supports: Dates Noether’s theorem on geometry and conservation to 1918.

caveats: The result has conditions: an arbitrary symmetry in an arbitrary system does not automatically produce a conserved quantity. Noether’s broader second theorem is not summarized in full.
